q.t: Find the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide (in cm).
q.e: Perimeter is the distance all the way round: two lengths and two breadths = 2 × (8 + 5) = 26.

q.t: Find the area of a square of side 7 cm (in cm²).
q.e: 7 rows of 7 unit squares: side × side = 49.

q.t: Find the area of a rectangle 12 m by 5 m (in m²).
q.e: 5 rows of 12 unit squares: length × breadth = 60.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a square of side 9 cm (in cm).
q.e: Four equal sides: 4 × 9 = 36.

q.t: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm (in cm²).
q.e: A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height: ½ × 10 × 6 = 30.

q.t: Find the area of a parallelogram with base 8 cm and height 5 cm (in cm²).
q.e: Cut the slanting triangle off one end and move it to the other — you get a rectangle 8 by 5. Area = base × height.

q.t: Find the circumference of a circle of diameter 14 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm.
q.e: Circumference = π × diameter = 22/7 × 14 = 44. The distance round any circle is a little over 3 times its width.

q.t: How many square centimetres make 1 square metre?
q.e: A square metre is 100 cm by 100 cm, so it holds 100 × 100 = 10,000 small squares.

q.t: A square has perimeter 48 cm. Find its side (in cm).
q.e: Four equal sides share 48 cm: 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

q.t: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm².
A rectangle has area 96 cm² and length 12 cm. Find its perimeter (in cm).
q.e: Breadth = 96 ÷ 12 = 8. Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 8) = 40.

q.t: A square has area 144 cm². Find its perimeter (in cm).
q.e: Side × side = 144, so the side is 12. Perimeter = 4 × 12 = 48.

q.t: A triangle has area 54 cm² and base 12 cm. Find its height (in cm).
A parallelogram has area 84 cm² and height 7 cm. Find its base (in cm).
q.e: Base × height = area, so base = 84 ÷ 7 = 12.

q.t: A circle has circumference 88 cm. Find its radius (take π = 22/7), in cm.
Find the area of a circle of diameter 28 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm².
q.e: Radius = 14 (half the diameter). Area = 22/7 × 14 × 14 = 616.

q.t: A rectangular field is 40 m by 25 m. Find the cost of fencing it at ₹12 per metre (in ₹).
q.e: Fencing goes round the edge, so use the perimeter: 2 × 65 = 130 m. Cost = 130 × 12 = 1560.

q.t: Find the area of a right-angled triangle whose legs are 9 cm and 12 cm (in cm²).
q.e: The two legs are at right angles, so one is the base and the other the height: ½ × 9 × 12 = 54.

q.t: A wheel has radius 35 cm. How far does it roll in one full turn (take π = 22/7), in cm?
q.e: One turn lays its whole rim on the ground once: circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 35 = 220.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: The diagonals cut the rhombus into 4 right triangles which fill half of a 10 × 24 rectangle: ½ × 10 × 24 = 120.

q.t: A garden 30 m by 20 m has a path 2 m wide all around it on the OUTSIDE. Find the area of the path (in m²).
q.e: The path adds 2 m at both ends of each side: outer rectangle 34 by 24 = 816. Path = 816 − 600 = 216.

q.t: How many square tiles of side 20 cm are needed to cover a floor 6 m by 4 m?
q.e: Use the same unit: floor 600 cm × 400 cm = 2,40,000 cm². Each tile = 400 cm². 2,40,000 ÷ 400 = 600.

q.t: A wheel has diameter 70 cm. How many full turns does it make in travelling 1.1 km (take π = 22/7)?
A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The square has side 15 cm and the rectangle is 18 cm long. How much greater is the square’s area (in cm²)?
q.e: Perimeter = 60, so the rectangle’s breadth is 30 − 18 = 12. Areas: 225 and 216. Difference 9. For a fixed perimeter the square holds the most.

q.t: Find the area of a ring between two circles with the same centre and radii 14 cm and 7 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm².
q.e: Big circle − small circle = 22/7 × (196 − 49) = 22/7 × 147 = 462.

q.t: A park 60 m by 40 m has two roads, each 5 m wide, crossing at the centre — one parallel to the length and one parallel to the breadth. Find the area covered by the roads (in m²).
q.e: Roads: 60 × 5 = 300 and 40 × 5 = 200. The 5 × 5 square where they cross was counted twice, so subtract 25: 475.

q.t: A parallelogram has sides 12 cm and 9 cm. The height on the 12 cm side is 6 cm. Find the height on the 9 cm side (in cm).
q.e: The area is the same whichever side is the base: 12 × 6 = 72 = 9 × h, so h = 8.

q.t: A wire shaped as a circle of radius 21 cm is bent into a square. Find the side of the square (take π = 22/7), in cm.
q.e: The wire’s length does not change: circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 21 = 132 cm. Side = 132 ÷ 4 = 33.

q.t: A triangle and a parallelogram have the same base and the same area. The parallelogram’s height is 6 cm. Find the triangle’s height (in cm).
q.e: Triangle area is HALF of base × height, so to match it needs twice the height: 12 cm.

q.t: Find the perimeter of a semicircular plate of radius 7 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm.
q.e: Curved part = half the circumference = 22/7 × 7 = 22. Add the straight edge (the diameter, 14): 36. Do not forget the straight edge.

q.t: A wire shaped as a square of side 22 cm is bent into a circle. Find the area of the circle (take π = 22/7), in cm².
q.e: Wire length = 4 × 22 = 88 cm = circumference, so r = 14. Area = 22/7 × 14 × 14 = 616 (more than the square’s 484).

q.t: The largest possible circle is cut from a square sheet of side 14 cm. Find the area of sheet left over (take π = 22/7), in cm².
q.e: The circle’s diameter equals the side, so r = 7. Square 196 − circle 154 = 42.

q.t: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and its breadth is decreased by 20%. Its area:
q.e: New area = 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96 of the old one — a 4% fall, because the 20% cut is taken from a longer side.

q.t: An isosceles right-angled triangle has area 50 cm². Find the length of each equal side (in cm).
q.e: The equal sides are the base and height: ½ × a × a = 50 → a² = 100 → a = 10.

q.t: A lawn 50 m by 30 m has a path 3 m wide all around it on the INSIDE. Find the area of the path (in m²).
q.e: The path takes 3 m off both ends of each side, leaving 44 by 24 = 1056. Path = 1500 − 1056 = 444.

q.t: The radii of two circles are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their areas?
q.e: Area depends on r², so the ratio is squared: 2² : 3² = 4 : 9.

q.t: The minute hand of a clock is 14 cm long. Find the area it sweeps in 15 minutes (take π = 22/7), in cm².
q.e: 15 minutes is a quarter of a full turn, so it sweeps a quarter of the circle: ¼ × 616 = 154.

q.t: A rhombus has perimeter 52 cm and one diagonal 24 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: Side = 13. Half-diagonals and a side make a right triangle: 13² − 12² = 25, so the other half-diagonal is 5 and that diagonal is 10. Area = ½ × 24 × 10 = 120.

q.t: A rectangle has perimeter 82 cm and area 400 cm². Find its length (in cm).
q.k: max(l for l in range(1,41) if l*(41-l)==400)
q.e: Length + breadth = 41 and length × breadth = 400. The pair 25 and 16 fits both (25 + 16 = 41, 25 × 16 = 400).

q.t: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 13 cm and base 10 cm. Find its area (in cm²).
q.e: The height bisects the base (5 and 5): 13² − 5² = 144, so the height is 12. Area = ½ × 10 × 12 = 60.
